> **In short.** In the context of the three runnable parts of ADR 0011, facing names that say where a part runs but
> not what it is, we decided for `company-server`, `companion` and `office-ui` and against keeping `server`, `client`
> and `web` or naming them after things in the office, to make every path explain itself, accepting a rename while the
> skeleton is still empty.

## Context and problem

ADR 0011 named the runnable parts `apps/server`, `apps/client` and `apps/web`; ADR 0004 point 7 and the Mechanics of
ADR 0012 name them too. The maintainer asked what the difference between client and web is: the names did not tell.
`client` is a Node process on a person's machine that serves the browser UI, connects to the company and runs that
person's AI employees through the official CLI; `web` is the office drawn in the browser tab, which can start no
process and read no file. Only the skeleton of PIX-7 uses the names so far.

## Decision drivers

- A path has to say what the part is, for contributors who read it the first time.
- An app's name must not be a word the domain uses, so a type in the core and an app never share a name.
- The command a person types, `npx pixecutive`, must not change.

## Considered options

- **A — Descriptive names:** `apps/company-server`, `apps/companion`, `apps/office-ui`.
- **B — Names from the office:** `company`, `desk`, `office`, `workshop`.
- **C — Keep** `server`, `client`, `web`.

## Decision

Chosen: **A** (maintainer, 2026-10-04), because it is the only option whose names say what each part is without
taking a word the domain needs.

1. **Apps are composition roots and driving adapters.** `apps/company-server` (one company instance, hosted) and
   `apps/companion` (the process `npx pixecutive` starts on a person's machine) wire ports to adapters and receive
   requests from HTTP, WebSocket or the command line. Wiring may use a dependency-injection container; where one binds
   a port, a token file names it. This restates ADR 0011 point 3 with the new names. `[Lint]`
2. **The browser UI stands outside the hexagon.** `apps/office-ui` never imports the core. The wire contract between
   the office UI, the companion and the company server lives in `packages/protocol` as zod schemas of the messages.
   This restates ADR 0011 point 4 with the new names. `[Lint]`
3. **Older ADRs keep their words; these names replace them.** Where ADR 0004, 0011 and 0012 say `apps/server`,
   `apps/client` or `apps/web`, the part is `apps/company-server`, `apps/companion` or `apps/office-ui`; product assets
   live under `apps/office-ui/assets/`. The published package stays `pixecutive`. `[Hook pre-commit]`

### Consequences

- Good, because each path explains itself and none collides with a domain word such as desk or office.
- Bad, because three older ADRs carry the old words in their text; their frontmatter points here.

### Confirmation

`check-images` in the pre-commit lets product assets in only under `apps/office-ui/assets/`; the import-zone probe of
PIX-7 plants an import of the core in `apps/office-ui` and turns red.

## Rejected

- **B — names from the office.** Desk and office are things in the domain; an app of the same name would make every
  conversation about them ambiguous.
- **C — keep the names.** They say where a part runs, not what it does, which is how the question arose.
